figures.caption: Table 3: Performance of restart strategies on interrupted runs. FPR = target false-positive rate threshold; FP lost = failed runs that would have passed without being aborted; TP rec. = recovered failing runs; Resolve rate = final success rate (parentheses show gains over uncontrolled baseline); Total token overhead denotes the net additional token spending after early-stop savings, as a percentage of standard singlesample spending. Ununitized values are in %; /t. = per task.

Table 12: Performance of the policy-specific early-stop monitors that produced the abort decisions consumed by RestartSmart (Table 3). Unlike Table 1, where a single monitor trained on 27B trajectories supervises every policy, each monitor here is trained on its own policy’s trajectories, the strongest abort signal available for restart. The Qwen3.627B block is identical to Table 1 by construction. Recall / Prec.: truly-failing runs aborted / aborted runs that are true failures; Fired / Saved: trajectories aborted / tokens reclaimed (all values in %). These policy-specific figures feed the restart experiments only; the headline token savings quoted in the abstract are those of the transferred monitor in Table 1.

Table 1: Early-stop monitor performance across false-positive rate (FPR) budgets. Recall: percentage of true failing runs flagged; Prec.: percentage of true failures among aborted runs; Fired / Saved: percentage of aborted trajectories and reclaimed tokens. Duration is a supervisor-free control given only the step count. Bold marks the best value of each metric per budget.
